capability_investigated:
generate(features, prompts, ...) signature and the WhisperFeatureExtractor
output shape — specifically whether the decode call accepts a batched
StorageView (N x n_mels x 3000) with a parallel prompt list rather than a
single 30s window.
what_i_learned:
The processor pads/truncates every input to a fixed 30s mel window, so the
stub silently dropped everything past the first 30 seconds of each call
(pure deletion). generate takes a list of prompts, so a batched feature
StorageView with one prompt per window decodes all segments in a single
call and returns one result per window.
hypothesis:
Split audio into ceil(len/30s) non-overlapping 30s windows, extract all
features at once, run one batched generate over [prompt]*N, and join the
per-window transcripts. This recovers the deleted tail and should sharply
raise length_ratio.p05 / cut the deletion rate that dominates the stub.

capability_investigated:
Re-examined generate()'s memory behavior on a batched StorageView: how peak
GPU allocation scales with the number of 30s windows passed in one decode
call (N x n_mels x 3000 features + N parallel beams).
what_i_learned:
generate() decodes all prompts in the list concurrently, so a single batched
call over every window of a long call allocates memory proportional to the
window count — long 0715 calls have enough windows to exceed GPU memory
(CUDA out of memory). Decoding one window per generate() call bounds peak
memory to a single 30s window and still recovers the full tail.
hypothesis:
Keep the long-form windowing that fixed the tail-deletion, but iterate the
windows through generate() one at a time instead of one giant batched call;
this removes the OOM crash while preserving the deletion fix, so the
iteration actually scores.

capability_investigated:
The WhisperGenerationResult object returned by frozen.generate() — specifically
its scores and no_speech_prob fields, and the return_scores /
return_no_speech_prob decode flags that populate them. Also the n-gram
blocking knob no_repeat_ngram_size on the decode call.
what_i_learned:
generate() exposes per-sequence avg log-prob (scores) and a per-window
no_speech_prob, but ONLY when return_scores=True / return_no_speech_prob=True
are passed — otherwise result.scores is empty and the signals are discarded.
This means coverage loss can be localized: every window IS decoded (loss isn't
at the chunker), so low length_ratio comes from individual windows collapsing
into repetition / early-EOS, detectable via low score + low unique-token ratio
while no_speech_prob stays low.
hypothesis:
Condition a fallback on those discarded signals: greedy-decode each window,
and only when its output is empty / score < -1.0 / repetitive AND
no_speech_prob < 0.6 (real speech present) re-decode once with beam_size=5 +
no_repeat_ngram_size=3 to break the loop and recover the deleted span. Targets
the dominant deletion axis without touching windows that already decode clean.

capability_investigated:
The decoder prompt fed to generate()'s `prompts` arg and Whisper's
timestamp-token vocabulary. Every prior iteration hard-coded
<|notimestamps|>, so the decode had never run in timestamped mode and the
emitted segment timestamps were never available.
what_i_learned:
Removing <|notimestamps|> from the prompt switches the backend into
timestamped decode: the returned sequences_ids carry timestamp tokens
(ids >= convert_tokens_to_ids("<|0.00|>"), spaced 0.02s), which
skip_special_tokens=True strips from the text but which can be read to find
where decoding stopped. This exposes the in-window stop position the
notimestamps regime hid, and the timestamp-trained decode is designed to walk
to the window end rather than early-EOS on long dense segments.
hypothesis:
In-window early truncation (len 0.66, del 82%) is the deletion source. Decode
each window with timestamps enabled, then advance the cursor to the last
emitted timestamp instead of a fixed 30s hop, so a window that stops early
gets its dropped tail re-decoded with context — recovering coverage at the
exact failure point, within the greedy runtime budget.

capability_investigated:
The decoder `prompts` arg fed to generate() — specifically Whisper's
previous-text context slot marked by <|startofprev|>, which precedes the
<|startoftranscript|> sot sequence. No iteration has put anything before
sot; the prompt has only ever been [sot, ko, transcribe].
what_i_learned:
generate()'s prompt token list accepts a previous-text segment before the
sot sequence: [<|startofprev|>] + prior_text_token_ids + [sot, ko,
transcribe]. Whisper conditions the decode on those prior tokens (the same
mechanism faster-whisper uses to carry context across long-form segments),
so cross-window context is an available, never-used input axis. Decoder
context is 448 tokens, bounding how much prior text can be prepended.
hypothesis:
Dominant axis is substitution (57%, coverage healthy at 0.95) → errors are
domain terms mis-recognized, and each 30s window currently decodes with zero
memory of the call. Carry the previous window's decoded text into the next
window as the <|startofprev|> prompt so the decoder is primed with running
call-center context and keeps domain vocabulary consistent across window
boundaries instead of independently re-guessing it.

capability_investigated:
generate()'s return value under beam search — specifically that sequences_ids
and scores are PARALLEL N-best lists (one entry per hypothesis), populated
only when beam_size>1 / num_hypotheses>1. Every prior iter decoded greedily
(beam_size=1) and read only sequences_ids[0], so the ranked alternatives the
call can return have never existed in this pipeline.
what_i_learned:
With beam_size=5, num_hypotheses=5, return_scores=True the WhisperGeneration
result exposes up to 5 ranked hypotheses with parallel avg-log-prob scores;
greedy decoding yields a degenerate 1-entry list and discards this entirely.
This gives both a search that can back out of a locally-wrong token (the
substitution lever) and an N-best set selectable by criteria other than the
beam's own score ranking.
hypothesis:
Substitution dominates (57%) with coverage already healthy — greedy commits
to locally-wrong tokens on domain/phone-band audio. Enable beam search and,
among hypotheses within a small score margin of the best, keep the one
reaching furthest into the window: beam search attacks substitution while the
completeness tie-break protects coverage without rewarding hallucinated length
(the insertion regression that sank iter5). Turbo's 4-layer decoder keeps
beam 5 within the runtime budget.

capability_investigated:
ctranslate2 Whisper.generate's avg-log-prob (result.scores, length-normalized
mean log-prob) and the sampling regime (beam_size=1, sampling_topk=0,
sampling_temperature>0) versus the beam regime — i.e. using the returned
score as a decode TRIGGER rather than only as a within-decode rerank key.
what_i_learned:
ct2's result.scores entry is already the length-normalized mean log-prob, the
exact quantity Whisper's reference decoder gates temperature-fallback on, so
it is directly comparable to the -1.0 log_prob_threshold. Sampling decode is
reachable through the frozen surface via beam_size=1 + sampling_topk=0 +
sampling_temperature>0, giving a stochastic re-decode the beam regime never
produces. Every prior iter consumed scores only to rerank N-best within one
decode and never to decide whether to re-decode.
hypothesis:
Add the canonical temperature-fallback loop: a window whose temp-0 beam decode
has avg_logprob < -1.0 (low confidence = substitution) or gzip
compression_ratio > 2.4 (repetition = hallucination, the two focus files'
failure) is re-decoded by sampling at higher temperatures, keeping the first
attempt clearing both gates. This escapes a wrong path the beam committed to
(substitution lever) and catches collapsed-into-filler windows (hallucination
lever) using a signal we always discarded.
